summary: Builds the Huffman decoding tables for the DEFLATE literal/length and distance code classes during inflate decompression setup. Allocates a 288-entry work buffer through an allocator function pointer on the inflate state object (a9), runs HuffmanCodingFrequencyTable once per code class using the static base/extra-bit tables (unk_5B0878/unk_5B08F8 for literal/length, unk_5B0978/unk_5B09F0 for distance), and writes DEFLATE error strings into the state object when the code-length data is oversubscribed, incomplete, or empty. Returns 0 on success, -4 on allocation failure, -3 on tree build errors.

operations.description: Initialize the local code-count/result accumulator v14 to 0 before any table build.
Allocate the 288 * 4 byte work table by calling the allocator function pointer stored at state offset a9+32 with the owner object at a9+40.
If the allocation returned NULL, return -4 immediately (no work buffer available).

Call HuffmanCodingFrequencyTable for the literal/length tree: code-length array a4, codes a3, count a1, 0x101u, base table unk_5B0878, extra-bits table unk_5B08F8, output table a6, extra arg a8, temp v14, and the freshly allocated work buffer v10.
Branch on the first table-build result v12; a non-zero return enters the literal/length error handling path.
If v12 == -3, write the error string "oversubscribed literal/length tree" into the state error slot at a9+24 and go to cleanup.
For any other failure (including -4 and the incomplete case), write "incomplete literal/length tree" into a9+24 and normalize the result to -3.
If the literal/length code-count *a4 is zero, treat the tree as incomplete literal/length and enter the error path.

Call HuffmanCodingFrequencyTable for the distance tree: code-length array a5, codes &a3[a1] (after the literal block), count a2, offset 0, base table unk_5B0978, extra-bits table unk_5B09F0, output table a7, extra arg a8, temp v14, and the same work buffer v15.
Switch on the distance table-build result v12: -3, -4, -5 and a default case each select a distance-tree error string.
On -3, write "oversubscribed distance tree" into the state error slot at a9+24.
On -5, write "incomplete distance tree" into a9+24 and force the result to -3.
On the default case, write "empty distance tree with lengths" into a9+24 and force the result to -3.
If the distance code-count *a5 is zero while a1 exceeds 0x101, treat the tree as an empty distance tree with lengths.
Success path: set the result v13 to 0.
Release the work buffer by calling the deallocator function pointer at state offset a9+36 with the owner object at a9+40.
Return v13 (0 on success, -4 on allocation failure, -3 on any tree build error).
